stories.headline: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
stories.title: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
stories.summary: Tokyo Nov 08: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media. Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported. A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu. Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee. The quake, which struck at 1:04 am local time, was located about 40 km below the earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighboring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments. The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on. Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes.

stories.title: How anti-AI trade after US midterm election results is reviving Indian, Chinese stocks
stories.summary: The unraveling of the AI trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favor Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.

Aberdeen Investments favors markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms.

stories.headline: Army intensifies LoC surveillance amid Diwali festivities, infiltration alert
stories.title: Army intensifies LoC surveillance amid Diwali festivities, infiltration alert
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 7: With Diwali celebrations underway across the country, Indian Army troops, deployed along the Line of Control (LoC) in Rajouri and Poonch, have intensified surveillance and security measures amid intelligence inputs suggesting possible infiltration attempts by terrorists and attempts to disturb peace during the festive season. In the Nowshera sector of Rajouri district, Army troops have stepped up foot patrolling, with teams maintaining round-the-clock vigilance to ensure effective domination of sensitive stretches along the LoC, particularly vulnerable locations that could potentially be exploited for infiltration. Besides ground surveillance, the Army is also using drones to monitor areas along the LoC, keeping a close watch on vulnerable routes and suspected infiltration corridors. A media visit was also conducted through Public Relations Unit Jammu at some forward LoC locations in Nowshera sector wherein the visiting journalists had a close understanding of Army's alertness. At LoC locations, Quick Reaction Teams (QRTs) have also been positioned at strategic locations to ensure an immediate response to any emerging situation. Equipped with armoured vehicles, these specialised teams remain on standby to move swiftly towards vulnerable spots whenever required. The multi-layered security arrangements, combining intensified foot patrolling, aerial surveillance and rapid response capabilities, are aimed at maintaining effective area domination and ensuring a high level of operational preparedness along the LoC during the festive period.

stories.headline: Who is Qiulae Wong? New Zealand's potential kingmaker after cliffhanger election
stories.title: Who is Qiulae Wong? New Zealand's potential kingmaker after cliffhanger election
stories.summary: Qiulae Wong, a 38-year-old politician who entered politics less than a year ago, could emerge as a kingmaker in New Zealand after the general election delivered no clear winner. Her centrist Opportunity Party is projected to win seven seats, potentially giving it a decisive role in government formation. Wong's party is pushing sweeping tax reforms, including a universal basic income funded by a land tax.

stories.headline: Pro-Poor Growth
stories.title: Pro-Poor Growth
stories.summary: Few economic statistics capture a nation's transformation as vividly as this one. According to the World Bank's October 2026 Poverty and Equity Brief, about 496 million Indians rose above the $4.20-a-day poverty line between 2011 and 2023, the benchmark for lower-middle-income economies. The headcount ratio of extreme poverty, measured at $3 a day in purchasing power parity terms, fell from 27.1% to 2.6%. In twelve years, India went from one in four citizens living in destitution to one in forty. It is among the fastest poverty reductions ever recorded. Nor is the World Bank alone. Its 2.6% is the highest of the recent estimates. Economists Surjit Bhalla and Karan Bhasin, writing for the Brookings Institution in 2024, put extreme poverty at about 2% and declared it eliminated, even without counting free rations. SBI Research estimated in early 2025 that overall poverty had fallen below 5%. Arvind Panagariya, chairman of the 16th Finance Commission, found that it fell from 21.9% to 2.3% by 2023-24 and called it virtually eliminated. Different poverty lines, different methods, one conclusion: extreme poverty in India is now close to zero. The engine was pro-poor growth. Real monthly per capita consumption expenditure rose by about 45% in rural India and 38% in urban India between 2011-12 and 2023-24. Crucially, the gains were largest at the bottom of the distribution: in 2023-24 alone, consumption among the poorest 5% of rural households grew about 22%. The consumption Gini coefficient fell in both rural and urban areas, and the urban-rural consumption gap narrowed from 84% to 70%. This is the textbook definition of inclusive growth: an expanding economy whose benefits reached those who needed them most. The growth elasticity of poverty tells the same story. A 43% rise in average real consumption was associated with a roughly 90% fall in extreme poverty, an elasticity of about minus two. Because millions of households were clustered just below the poverty line, broad-based income growth carried them across it in large numbers. Rural demand, long the weak link in India's growth story, became its driving force. Labour markets amplified the effect. Employment expanded by about 134 million between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the growth of the working-age population, with rural women entering paid work in unprecedented numbers. More earners per household meant higher household consumption, even in years when real wages moved slowly. Public investment in human capital and basic services did the rest. Toilets, clean cooking fuel, electricity, housing, piped water and bank accounts reached poor households at a scale few developing countries have attempted. Multidimensional poverty, which measures deprivation beyond income, fell from about 29% to 11% in under a decade. Financial inclusion through Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and mobile phones built the digital rails for direct benefit transfers, reducing leakages and putting resources straight into beneficiaries' hands. A food security net covering about 81 crore people provided a consumption floor that proved decisive during the pandemic, when a temporary income shock could otherwise have pushed millions back into poverty. Improvements in statistical measurement have also played a part. India's redesigned Household Consumption Expenditure Survey captures spending more accurately, and the World Bank's updated purchasing power parities reflect India's price levels better. These refinements make the data more reliable. They do not change the direction of travel, which every independent estimate confirms. The policy agenda now shifts from eliminating destitution to building prosperity. India should adopt an official national poverty line based on the new survey, so that progress is measured on its own terms. The focus must move to productivity: labour-intensive manufacturing, rural non-farm enterprise and skills that turn new jobs into better-paid ones, especially for the millions of women who have joined the workforce. Welfare can now evolve from a broad safety net into a targeted ladder, with a stronger emphasis on nutrition, health and education to deepen human capital. And as India approaches the $8.30 benchmark used for upper-middle-income economies, the ambition should rise with it. India has achieved one of the defining goals of the Sustainable Development Goals well ahead of 2030. The world spent decades asking whether growth in a large, diverse democracy could reach the poor. India's answer, written in the consumption data of half a billion people, is a resounding yes. Lokesh Dhar is a public policy consultant.

stories.headline: Defence Minister asks armed forces to maintain high operational readiness, counter cyber and drone threats
stories.title: Defence Minister asks armed forces to maintain high operational readiness, counter cyber and drone threats
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 7: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday called upon the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, with particular focus on domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats. Interacting with Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel at Air Force Station Bagdogra in West Bengal on the eve of Diwali, he said the security environment had become increasingly complex, with warfare extending beyond conventional border engagements to include asymmetric warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone swarms and information operations. He cautioned that adversaries were increasingly avoiding direct confrontation and attempting to exploit vulnerabilities through misleading information and social media campaigns. “Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information. In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier,” he said. Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important location and a crucial link in India’s security framework, particularly for the North-Eastern region, Rajnath Singh praised the courage and dedication of the personnel deployed there. He said the Air Warriors stationed in the region served as a strong shield for the security of the eastern sector and that their preparedness was essential for maintaining regional stability. The Defence Minister also stressed that discipline and courage remained indispensable despite rapid technological advancements. He said the conduct, language and restraint of armed forces personnel shaped the military’s image among local communities. Urging the personnel to strengthen their engagement with people in and around Bagdogra, he said building public trust was equally important for national security. “The more you engage with the local community, the weaker the adversary’s conspiracies will become,” he said. Reaffirming the government’s commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Rajnath Singh highlighted the growing contribution of Indian start-ups and industries to the development of drones, anti-drone systems and advanced military equipment. He appreciated the armed forces for adopting indigenous technologies and acquiring new skills in drone operations and cyber security, emphasising that the military must become increasingly technology-driven to meet future challenges. Referring to the Cabinet’s approval of the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ for Agniveers, the Defence Minister said the decision would provide them another opportunity to serve the country. He said that after completing the two-year engagement period, all Agniveers would have an opportunity to be enrolled as regular soldiers, subject to their willingness and fulfilment of selection criteria. He described the decision as a significant Diwali gift for Agniveers. Rajnath Singh also extended Diwali greetings to the Air Warriors and their families, acknowledging the sacrifices made by personnel who remain away from their homes during festivals to protect the country. He expressed gratitude to their families for their contribution and assured them that the nation would always stand by them and look after their welfare. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station Bagdogra, Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior IAF officials were present on the occasion.

stories.headline: Amit Shah reviews Gujarat’s internal security, directs action against drug networks, illegal migrants
stories.title: Amit Shah reviews Gujarat’s internal security, directs action against drug networks, illegal migrants
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 7: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday reviewed the law and order and internal security situation in Gujarat at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad, directing security agencies to strengthen coastal and border surveillance and intensify action against drug trafficking, cybercrime and illegal migration. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, Union Home Secretary and senior officials of the Union Home Ministry and Gujarat government attended the meeting. Several key issues, including border and coastal security, implementation of new criminal laws, drug trafficking, cybercrime, terrorism, illegal migration and disaster management, were discussed. Taking note of Gujarat’s nearly 2,340-km-long coastline and its international border with Pakistan, Shah stressed the need for stronger surveillance and better coordination among the Border Security Force (BSF), state police, Coast Guard and central agencies. Appreciating the state’s performance in implementing the new criminal laws, Shah said 92 per cent of chargesheets in Gujarat were filed within 60 days and 86 per cent within 90 days. He, however, directed the state government to launch a special drive to clear more than 25,000 pending forensic cases. On drug trafficking, the Home Minister said action should not be limited to small-time peddlers but must target the entire network and its main kingpins. He also called for prioritising financial investigations to identify and seize their illicit assets. Shah directed authorities to strengthen the capacity of the State Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (S4C) and the 1930 cybercrime helpline. He also called for strengthening counter-terrorism agencies and expediting the identification and deportation of illegal foreign nationals in accordance with the law. He appreciated Gujarat’s efforts in deporting 2,412 illegal foreign nationals during special drives. The meeting also reviewed disaster management, fire safety, the Ahmedabad Urban Flood Management Project and the survey and disposal of enemy properties. At the conclusion of the meeting, Shah directed Central and state agencies to work in close coordination and regularly review progress against prescribed targets. He reiterated the commitment to building a secure India through a safe, developed and drug-free Gujarat.
